rv.q: He is, without doubt, a magnificent performer at the height of his powers and this new play, transferring from the Sam Wanamaker Playhouse at the Globe, offers him an easy chance to shine once more.

It’s almost a theatrical rebuff but it draws us into a borderline psychological state twixt sleep and wake, lucidity and incomprehension, jest and earnest that has us – like Philippe’s exasperated adherents – hanging on every word.
Rylance’s loony melancholic leader finds him at his most delicate and ethereal, and clownish.

cn.t: Rylance delivers a captivating, delicate performance in his wife's beguiling play about music and royal madness, though the drama loses some focus in its second half.
